claims.text: The target nanoparticles contain five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios.
The initial nanoparticles are single-phase solid solutions with a uniform elemental distribution.
The initial nanoparticles exhibit slight short-range chemical ordering.
An atomic-size-difference threshold of approximately 15% is an acceptable limit for maintaining a solid solution.
Atomic-size disparity is a governing criterion for single-phase solid-solution formation or stability.
A sufficiently favorable or negative mixing enthalpy allows configurational entropy to dominate and favor random mixing over ordering.
High configurational entropy stabilizes a disordered, well-mixed solid solution.
Lattice distortion increases the effective energy barrier for atomic diffusion.
Lattice distortion increases the effective temperature by enhancing atomic diffusion barriers.
Higher diffusion barriers retard the long-range diffusion required for chemical segregation and phase separation.
The combined effects of configurational entropy and lattice distortion maintain structural and chemical stability throughout 473–1923 K.
HEA nanoparticles can retain similar structures from 573 to 1000 K and exhibit catalytic durability.
The proposed stability mechanism applies at thermoelectric operating temperatures up to 1923 K.
Greater atomic-size dispersion above the proposed threshold will promote chemical segregation or ordered/intermetallic phase formation.
At fixed composition, samples with less pronounced lattice distortion will segregate or form ordered/intermetallic phases more readily.
Controlled annealing can produce otherwise comparable samples with distinct levels of lattice distortion.
External chemical or mechanical perturbations can create additional diffusion pathways that invalidate the prediction.
Processing kinetics may influence phase stability outcomes.

contradictions.description: The prediction says that less pronounced lattice distortion should lead to segregation or ordered phases, but the falsification rule says that extensive separation in a low-distortion sample would falsify the hypothesis. That observation is presented both as an expected result and as a falsifier.

The hypothesis invokes an increased effective energy barrier that suppresses diffusion, whereas the mechanism says lattice distortion increases the effective temperature. Increasing effective temperature conventionally implies enhanced thermal activation, making this wording inconsistent with the claimed diffusion retardation.
